topic: Equality of quantum and general spin-one rotation correlations for arbitrary finite outcome sets
title: Answering the finite-outcome question of Aloy et al. (2024), arXiv:2312.09278v2, end of §IV.B.3, p. 17: an extension of their binary spin-one theorem

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending the binary-outcome theorem of Aloy, Galley, Jones, Ludescher and Müller (2024), we answer yes to their unnumbered question at the end of §IV.B.3 of arXiv:2312.09278v2, p. 17 (§IV.2.3 in the arXiv HTML): quantum and general spin-one rotation correlations coincide for every finite outcome set with at least three elements. Reversal-transpose averaging preserves each positive Gram polynomial and makes the total Gram matrix diagonal. Diagonal normalization yields one pure qutrit state and one POVM for the complete probability family, including singular boundary cases.
summary: Every normalized finite family of nonnegative degree-two trigonometric probability polynomials has a pure qutrit realization with balanced outer-frequency populations. Written corollaries give the lower-spin equalities, exact spin-one positive-Gram feasibility, dimension-three optimality, the obstruction to a universal fixed state, stochastic postprocessing, and the failure of reversal averaging alone to force a diagonal sum at degree three.
